environmental: relating to the natural world or surrounding conditions
New environmental rules limit factory emissions near rivers.
charges: fills a battery with electrical energy
The phone charges fully in under an hour with the new adapter.
reduce: to make something smaller or less in amount
The government hopes to reduce traffic congestion in the city centre.
demand: to require or need something firmly
Modern customers demand fast and reliable delivery service.
little: There is little time left before the deadline arrives.
importantly: in a manner that matters greatly; used to add a significant point
The plan is affordable and, importantly, easy to maintain.
raise: to increase the amount, level, or position of something
The landlord decided to raise the rent again this year.
cleaning: the act of removing dirt from something
Cleaning the gutters is an annual task before the rainy season.
monitoring: the act of watching and checking something over time
The agency is responsible for monitoring air quality across the city.
critics: people who express disapproval or judge the faults of something
nhà phê bình, người chỉ trích
Critics praised the novel's honest portrayal of grief.
point: Mark the point where the two roads meet on the map.
make: to produce, create or cause something
Good lighting can make a small room feel much larger.
famous: The city is famous for its ancient temples.
feel: to sense or experience something physically or emotionally
You can feel the ground shake when a train passes by.
reserved: kept back for a particular person or purpose
The front seats are reserved for elderly passengers.
travellers: plural of traveller; people who travel
Critics point out that fees can make a famous place feel reserved for richer travellers.
supporters: people who back or agree with a cause, team or person
Supporters gathered outside the stadium before the final.
reply: an answer given in response to something
His reply to the invitation arrived a week later.
test: a procedure used to check or examine something
She passed her driving test on the very first attempt.
whether: used to express doubt or choice between alternatives
The useful question is not whether a task is hard, but how it is done.
actually: in fact; really, contrary to what might be expected
The film was actually shot in a different country than the story suggests.
returns: The bird returns to the same nest every spring.
site: a place where something is located or where an event takes place
Archaeologists discovered ancient pottery at the excavation site.
third: coming after the second in a sequence; one of three equal parts
She finished the race in third place.
approach: a way of dealing with or thinking about something
The teacher tried a new approach to make grammar lessons more fun.
tries: present tense of try, used with he/she/it; makes an attempt
A third approach tries to spread visitors out rather than turn them away.
rather: She chose to walk rather than take the crowded bus.
away: to or at a distance from a place or person
The children ran away when they saw the dog.
tourist: relating to tourism or visitors travelling for pleasure
Tourist boards promote the quiet months and offer discounts outside holidays.
boards: groups of people who manage or promote an organization
Several tourist boards launched new campaigns to attract spring visitors.
promote: to help something become more popular or successful
The city launched a campaign to promote cycling instead of driving.
quiet: making little or no noise; calm
The library is usually quiet enough for deep concentration.
months: periods that a year is divided into, plural of month
It took several months for the wound to heal completely.
offer: to present something for someone to accept or refuse
The bank offered him a loan with a low interest rate.
discounts: reductions in the usual price of something
The store offers discounts on winter clothing every January.
outside: not inside; in or to a place beyond the boundary of something
The children played outside until it grew dark.
holidays: periods of rest from work or school, plural
Flights get expensive during the summer holidays.
advertise: to promote a product, service, or event publicly
Local shops often advertise their sales in the weekend newspaper.
nearby: not far away; close at hand
We found a nearby café that served excellent coffee.
few: a small number of; not many
Only a few students finished the exam before the bell rang.
heard: perceived sound with the ears; past tense of hear
She heard footsteps approaching from behind the door.
crowd: a large group of people gathered together
A crowd gathered outside the stadium hours before kickoff.
visits: goes to see a person or place
If part of the crowd visits in a different season, the pressure eases.
different: not the same as another or each other
Every student in the class has a different learning style.
season: one of the main periods of the year, or a period of a particular activity
Mango season brings extra income to farmers each year.
pressure: a feeling of stress caused by demands or difficulties
The manager felt under pressure to finish the project by Friday.
falls: Temperature falls sharply after sunset in the desert.
anyone: Anyone interested in the workshop should sign up before Friday.
being: existing, or the fact of existing in a particular state
Being tired all week, she decided to cancel her weekend plans.
told: past tense of tell; communicated information to someone
A vessel sitting well above its red band is empty, and anyone can see that without being told.
sometimes: on some occasions but not always
Sometimes she walks to work instead of driving.
dramatic: sudden and striking; exciting or impressive
The city saw a dramatic rise in temperature this summer.
option: a thing that may be chosen from a set of possibilities
Renting is often a cheaper option than buying for young families.
used: past tense of use; employed something for a purpose
A language kept only in books can be studied but not used.
closing: shutting, or coming to an end
Closing the shop early gave staff time to rest before the holiday.
completely: The old factory was completely rebuilt after the fire.
well-known: One well-known beach was shut to visitors after its coral was damaged.
beach: an area of sand or stones beside the sea
Families gathered on the beach to watch the sunset.
southern: located in or relating to the south of an area
Southern regions of the country tend to have warmer winters.
thailand: They spent two weeks travelling through northern Thailand.
made: The table was made entirely from reclaimed wood.
by: indicating the agent, method, or proximity of something
The letter was written by hand and delivered by courier.
film: The film won several awards at the festival.
shut: to close something, or to stop operating
The factory will shut permanently at the end of this year.
several: more than two but not very many
Several guests arrived late because of the traffic.
after: following in time or place; later than
The shop stays open late after the holiday season begins.
had: past tense of have, used to show possession or a completed action
By the time she arrived, the shop had already closed.
badly: in a poor or unsatisfactory way
The team played badly in the first half of the match.
reopened: The museum reopened after months of renovation.
were: past tense of 'be', used for plural or 'you'
The missing words had to be invented, and many were.
longer: for a greater length of time
Fresh bread stays soft for longer if wrapped properly.
into: moving towards the inside of something
She walked into the room and switched on the light.
swimming: the activity of moving through water using the body
Swimming is her favourite way to relax after a long week.
restricted: Access to the archive is restricted to registered researchers.
limited: restricted in amount, extent, or scope
The museum has only limited space for new exhibits.
closure: the act of shutting something, or bringing something to an end
The closure of the factory affected hundreds of local jobs.
expensive: The engine burns more fuel, and on a long voyage that becomes expensive.
shows: makes clear or proves that something is true
The evidence shows a clear link between smoking and lung disease.
nature: the basic or inherent character of a person or thing; the physical world
It is human nature to notice bad news more than good news.
given: provided or handed over to someone
Every student was given a copy of the new textbook.
enough: as much or as many as needed
There was barely enough food to feed everyone at the table.
none: not any of a group of people or things
None of the students had heard of the composer before.
these: used to refer to people or things nearby or just mentioned
These shoes are far more comfortable than my old ones.
methods: Farmers are adopting new methods to conserve water during droughts.
works: This explains why rereading notes feels productive and works so poorly.
limits: the greatest amounts or extents allowed
Every method of measuring risk has its own limits.
enforcement: the process of making sure rules or laws are obeyed
Weak enforcement meant the ban was widely ignored.
ignored: paid no attention to something deliberately, past tense
Her advice was ignored until it was too late.
transparency: the quality of being open, clear, and easy to understand or see through
Fees without transparency create distrust among visitors.
create: cause something new to exist; bring into being
The chef wanted to create a dish that combined two very different cuisines.
distrust: a lack of trust or confidence in someone
Years of broken promises left deep distrust among the villagers.
low-season: the period when demand, especially tourism, is lowest
Hotels cut their prices sharply during the low-season months.
campaigns: plural of campaign; organized efforts to achieve a goal
The city ran several campaigns to encourage recycling among residents.
change: A single ingredient can change the whole flavour of a dish.
habits: things done regularly, almost without thinking
Good sleeping habits make a noticeable difference to concentration.
tied: bound, fastened, or restricted to something
A community that could not was tied to whatever it could catch or grow that week.
manage: to succeed in doing something difficult; to control or direct
She had to manage a busy restaurant on her own that night.
best: of the highest quality or most excellent
This bakery makes the best bread in the whole neighbourhood.
combine: to join two or more things together to form a single thing
The recipe asks you to combine flour, sugar and butter first.
tools: plural of tool; devices used to carry out tasks
It has no words for the small things like kitchen tools or playground arguments.
crucially: in a way that is extremely important, especially to an outcome
The plan worked because, crucially, everyone understood their role.
involve: to include or require something as a necessary part
cho tham gia vào, bao gồm
The new job will involve frequent travel to other cities.
residents: people who live in a particular place
Local residents complained about the noise from the new bar.
deciding: making a choice or judgment after considering options
The judge spent weeks deciding how to rule on the complex case.
most: the majority of; the greatest amount or number of
Most of the guests had already left by the time the rain started.
useful: able to be used effectively for a purpose; helpful
The useful question is not whether a task is hard, but whether anyone can say how it is done.
success: the achievement of a desired aim or result
Her hard work eventually led to great success in business.
measured: found the size, amount, or degree of something
Researchers measured the temperature of the water every hour.
destination: the place someone or something is traveling to
Paris remains one of the most popular travel destinations in Europe.
judged: formed an opinion about something after consideration
The competition was judged by a panel of five experts.
arrived: reached a place or came to happen
The package finally arrived after two weeks of waiting.
better: of higher quality or more suitable than something else
The second recipe turned out much better than the first attempt.
visitor: a person who visits a place or person
Each visitor is asked to sign the guest book at the entrance.
leaves: goes away from a place, or allows something to remain (he/she/it)
The train leaves the station every hour on the hour.
behind: at or toward the back of something
She parked the car behind the old warehouse near the river.
both: the two of something, referring to two things together
Both students finished the exam well before the time limit.
landscape: the visible features of an area of land
Wind turbines have changed the landscape along the coast.
welcomes: A bay that welcomes fewer boats may keep its water cleaner in the long run.
fewer: Fewer people are buying newspapers than a decade ago.
clean: He always keeps his workshop spotlessly clean.
run: to move quickly, or to continue moving under its own momentum
The car will run for a while even after the engine dies.
goal: an aim or desired result that someone works towards
Her main goal this year is to save enough money to travel.
less: He eats less meat now than he used to.
survive: to continue to live or exist, especially after a difficulty
Few of the original buildings managed to survive the great fire.
